ops.body:
New evidence, 2026-07-30, commit 1067b25 (cut phase 0 — purely additive).

The daemon package failed twice in a row on macos-latest, with a DIFFERENT test each time:
  run 1: TestProductSettlementTimeoutIsStickyAndRetainsLowerOwnership (daemon/product_settlement_test.go:154)
         "worker: standard input delivery failed: write |1: broken pipe"
  run 2: TestRuntimeLifecycleSequenceEdges/Max-1_Commit_fatal_still_makes_Close_join

Different test per run, same package, all spawn-dependent — the recorded signature.

PROOF the commit is not the cause, stronger than the usual import-graph argument: `go list` shows
the daemon package and its tests import only realhome, runtimeauth, peer, proc, trust and worker
from this module. Not the root package, not internal/state, and not paths (nothing outside paths
imports paths). The new code is therefore not even LINKED into the daemon test binary. Absent
code cannot fail a test.

Measured pass rate on main, last 20 ci.yml runs: 15 success / 3 failure / 2 cancelled (~83%).
Two consecutive failures at a ~17% base rate is ~3% likely — unlucky, and the mechanism proof
overrides the statistics.

Why this matters beyond triage: a gate that reds a meaningful fraction of clean pushes trains
everyone to re-run without reading, which is exactly how 18,999 handshake failures hid behind
green CI for five days. That makes this a CI-credibility problem, not just a flaky test.

Root cause is unchanged and now measured directly (cc-notes note a40a3a1): every daemonkit child
spawns through exec.Command("/bin/sh", ...) at proc/manager.go:1139, and the trust verifier child
adds an unsigned os.Executable() re-exec on top. Fork/exec latency on a loaded host measured
0.00s to 13.66s for the same trivial spawn.

The rewrite deletes both causes independently — the /bin/sh gate becomes
POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED, and peer verification becomes kernel-only with no child at all
(note bfc1789) — so this closes as a consequence of phases 1-2 rather than needing its own fix.
